doc.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016

title: Maurice White, Earth Wind & Fire and David Bowie
summary: He praises Earth Wind & Fire's That's the Way of the World, and compares Bowie to Bilal as character singers.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I have one or two more questions. For the record, you’ve covered David Bowie songs, he just passed. Maurice White Earth Wind & Fire just passed. Speak about those two in terms of your thoughts about them in particular.
Oh yeah. I mean Maurice White is you know, they were doing, not hip-hop and jazz, but they were doing funk and soul and jazz.
Everything. There’s an album “That’s the Way of the World.”
“That’s the Way of the World.” That still to this day that has to be one of my favorite interludes of all times.

No. It’s “Interlude” after oh I forgot the song it’s after. But it’s a [scats]. Anyway they were ahead of their time for that. That “Interlude” it’s literally my favorite interlude ever. It’s like 45 seconds and it’s so dope. You know. And they way they did it was dope and ahead of their time the way they did it too. They took something and flipped it, they took something, another song of theirs, “Celebration,” and flipped it and flipped the tape and made it go backwards. And then Bobby Lyle soloed over it going forward. It was like, “really, that’s what you’re going to do?” And it was so crazy. And on the same album they have a jazz interlude, I forget what it’s called, something jazz. But they just walk in the studio and you hear them giving them a set and they start playing, it’s like a blues or something. But then it goes into “The Way of the World.” You know what I mean? And that was just normal back then. And I mean I knew that record for a long time because my mom used to play that all the time and my dad used to play it all the time. You know what I mean? So that’s one of the things I would hear, and just like that’s normal. Jazz, going to this, what’s the problem? You know what I mean? David Bowie, you know who reminds me of David Bowie? Bilal. He reminds me of David Bowie a lot. Artistically, Bilal’s weird and so is David Bowie, super-weird. And they’re very much, they play characters when they sing. It’s not about — a lot of singers, every time they sing it’s like let me show you how good I sing. I don’t care what the song’s about, I don’t care about selling the song to you, I want you to know I can sing very good. You know. And some singers are about characters and being a character for that song, like it’s a part. You know what I mean? And trying to tell a story. Prince is one of those people. You know what I mean? Bilal’s one of those. David Bowie’s one of those to me. David Bowie could really sing. But that wasn’t his point. You would catch it. Because he’s really dope. But that wasn’t his main thing.
